old: dek: "A Cabinet Office working group proposed binding safety and incident-reporting rules for widely used frontier AI providers on November 27, 2026, replacing voluntary guidance with corrective orders."
new: dek: "A Cabinet Office working group proposed binding safety and incident-reporting rules for widely used frontier AI providers on November 27, 2026, adding corrective orders alongside voluntary guidance."
why: The draft summary keeps Japan's soft-law voluntary guideline framework in principle while adding binding duties and corrective orders for high-risk frontier AI services.

support.quote: 1. 今後の制度の検討の在り方 以上のとおり、令和 7 年のＡＩ法制定以降の情勢を踏まえれば、原則として、既存の法令や ガイドライン等のソフトローを適切に組み合わせＡＩのリスクに対応していくという、これま での我が国における基本的な考え方は維持しつつ、既存の法令やソフトローのみでは対応が困 難な重大なリスクについては、早急に法整備を行い、一部のＡＩサービス提供者に対し法律上 の義務を課すことで、ＡＩの安全を確保していくことが必要であると考えられる。

old: Qualifying operators would also be required to report serious adverse impacts or concrete risks to the state and respond to government information requests, with on-site inspections reserved for cases where reporting alone is insufficient.[^2]
new: Qualifying operators would also be required to report serious adverse impacts or concrete risks to the state and respond to government information requests, while whether to include on-site inspections—limited to cases where reporting proves insufficient—remains under study.[^2]
why: Section III.2.(3) of the draft summary says whether to establish an on-site inspection provision should still be examined, rather than presenting inspections as settled.

old: It also says that requiring providers to publish how they apply their safety measures could be considered, with care not to expose trade secrets or information that could invite misuse.[^2]
new: It also says requiring providers to publish how they implement safety measures could be considered, alongside a provision to publicize facts when authorities exercise enforcement powers without exposing trade secrets or information inviting misuse.[^2]
why: The trade-secret and misuse caveat in Section III.2.(4) applies to publicizing facts when authorities exercise recommendation or order powers, distinct from Section III.2.(1) on provider safety disclosures.
